class.name: JarBodyClouds
class.brief_description: Volumetric clouds above the body's sea level.
class.description: A layer of clouds between [member altitude] and [member altitude] + [member thickness] meters above sea level (a spherical shell, or a slab on a flat body). Where clouds are comes from the planet's weather map, made in C++ at startup (a cube map, about half a second, no baking; [member seed]): climate zones with noisy borders (storm clusters along the equator, mostly clear subtropics with fields of trade cumulus and cellular low cloud, cyclones with spiral arms and fronts drawn out east to west in the storm belts, stratus over the poles), how high the tops reach and how sheet-like they are. It drifts slowly around the planet. The clouds are one model at every distance, so nothing switches as you climb or descend: the weather map, then regions (smooth noise stretched east-west: clusters, gaps and streets, the material's [code]region_size[/code] and [code]region_strength[/code]), then single clouds (Perlin-Worley noise, [code]cloud_size[/code]), then eroded detail. Each scale fades out where it is smaller than a pixel and is replaced by its average (the covered fraction of the pixel), and the step count follows what a pixel resolves, so a planet full of clouds seen from afar costs little. Lit through the cloud towards the sun with silver linings, approximate multiple scattering, darker edges facing away from the sun, sky light and the planet's shadow; at night through the cloud towards the moon (or the starlit sky above), so undersides stay dark. Over time the clouds grow and dissolve in place (the material's [code]evolution[/code]) and the weather changes ([member weather_period]). Faint wisps, which are mostly noise on screen, are dropped by the material's [code]faint_cutoff[/code] (clouds keep their size). They are ray marched by [JarCloudsEffect], a compositor effect, at half resolution (one pixel of each 2x2 block per frame) and accumulated over frames through the body's own space, then put on screen at full resolution by the layer's material, after the water and the atmosphere, hazed by the body's [JarBodyAtmosphere] only as far as the clouds are (the material's render priority must be above the atmosphere's 100). The layer adds a [JarCloudsEffect] to the scene's [WorldEnvironment] (or camera) compositor if there is none. Beyond the far plane they are drawn in scaled space with the rest of the body. Coverage, sizes, density, wind, colors and quality are set on [member material].

method.name: get_weather
method.description: The weather map in use (a [Cubemap]: r coverage, g how high the tops reach, b how sheet-like), made at the layer's first update; null on flat bodies.

method.name: get_active_material
method.description: The material in use: [member material] or the default.

method.name: get_detail_noise
method.description: The detail noise in use (a 64 texel [Texture3D] of Worley noise that erodes the clouds' edges), null until it is made (a fraction of a second, on a thread).

method.name: get_shape_noise
method.description: The shape noise in use (a 128 texel [Texture3D]: r Perlin-Worley for single clouds, g smooth noise for regions), null until it is made (a fraction of a second, on a thread).

method.name: get_view_scale
method.description: How much smaller the clouds are drawn: 1 near, less in scaled space.

method.name: get_world_to_body
method.description: From the scene's orientation to the body's, as of the last update: the clouds turn with the body.

members.member: Height of the bottom of the cloud layer above sea level, in meters.

Seconds each weather map shows. A new one (made on a thread from [member seed] and its number) fades in over the last 40 percent of that time, and while it shows each map is drawn out by zonal winds (the material's [code]zonal_wind[/code]): weather systems form, move and dissolve. 0: one map that only drifts.
Which weather: the weather map is made from it (cyclones, cloud fields).
Height of the layer from its bottom to its top, in meters.
The clouds' look. Empty: the default [code]clouds.gdshader[/code].
